display.title: Rabbi Akiva's Negel Vasser, Ahavas Yisroel and the Drunken Father
display.summary_short: Three-part story time from the Three Weeks: Rabbi Akiva washes negel vasser in prison, his 'great rule' of loving others, and a story with no happy ending about copying bad ways.
display.summary_long: A long story block from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded during the Three Weeks. First, Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days, uses his jug of water to wash negel vasser and make a brachah; the amazed ruler frees him and makes him an advisor. Uncle Yossi then explains Rabbi Akiva's teaching that loving your fellow as yourself is a great rule of the Torah, and the Alter Rebbe's words that Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem: to love Hashem, we love those He loves. Since the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed for lack of Ahavas Yisroel, this matters most in the Three Weeks. Finally comes a story that 'has no happy ending'. Naftali, a fine, respectful boy, is ashamed that his father drinks too much. He leads his father to a drunk lying in the street, hoping he will see how awful it is, but the father only asks where to get such a good drink. Like the Torah's warning in Parshas Acharei not to follow the ways of Egypt and Canaan, we are shown bad ways only so that we reject them and set an example.
display.lesson: Keep mitzvos with firm belief, love every Jew, and learn from bad examples what not to copy.
